knobs.why: The thing under test. Different model, different experiment.
llm_agent is the plain ReAct-ish loop. llm_agent_solo/llm_agent_gt are ablations that remove the user or hand over an oracle plan.
tau2 runs 0.0. Sampling temperature is a confound across arms.
The user sim IS half the environment: it decides what gets revealed, when, and when to say ###STOP###. A weaker user sim caps the agent's achievable reward. Arm A must drive the same simulator model.
dummy_user is the no-user ablation; user_simulator is the real one.
retail ships base(114) / train(74) / test(40). Comparing a test-split Arm A against a base-split Arm B compares different task mixes.
The join is per task_id, so any task present in one arm and absent from the other must be dropped explicitly, not averaged over.
pass^k is only defined at equal k. Mean reward over 1 trial and over 4 trials are different estimators with different variance.
The truncation budget. A tighter budget converts solvable tasks into max_steps terminations, which score 0.
Consecutive tool-error budget before the run is abandoned.
Seeds the per-trial seeds. Same seed does NOT make LLM sampling deterministic, but it does keep trial indexing aligned.
Pins the domain DB, the tool implementations and the evaluator. Arm A's world was exported from this tree.

The scoring contract itself, not a version knob. DB+COMMUNICATE and DB+NL_ASSERTION grade different things (the paper-era artifacts shipped with this repo were scored under the former; this pinned checkout scores retail under the latter on 112/114 base tasks). A pass rate computed under one basis is not comparable to a pass rate computed under the other no matter how well every other knob lines up, so this is checked even when --allow-commit-drift is passed.

problems: reward_basis: artifact was scored under {'COMMUNICATE,DB': 114} but the pinned tau2 checkout (5ebebbe827b4) grades these same 114 task ids under {'DB': 2, 'DB,NL_ASSERTION': 112} today -- these are different scoring metrics (e.g. DB+COMMUNICATE vs DB+NL_ASSERTION), so a pass rate under one is not comparable to a pass rate under the other; --allow-commit-drift does not waive this
